distillation_scope_note: Disease-specific medical input is limited to the disease name: Myxedema coma. Cause, trigger, central versus primary thyroid physiology, infection overlap, sedative exposure, cold exposure, cardiac phenotype, adrenal reserve, and organ-failure severity are represented only as axes, mechanism edges, risk/context factors, event hazards, treatment modifiers, or case evidence.

latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Markedly insufficient circulating thyroxine and triiodothyronine effect, usually longstanding and then clinically decompensated by physiologic stress, medication interruption, cold exposure, or another trigger.
Reduced thyroid hormone action lowers mitochondrial thermogenesis, cardiac chronotropy, ventilatory drive, neuromuscular function, renal free-water clearance, and gastrointestinal motility.

Low metabolic heat production and impaired adaptive response create hypothermia or absent fever despite infection; hypothermia worsens bradycardia, coagulopathy, respiratory drive, and drug clearance.
Reduced cerebral metabolism, hypothermia, hyponatremia, hypoglycemia, hypercapnia, sedative sensitivity, and trigger illness produce somnolence, delirium, stupor, seizure risk, or coma.

Depressed ventilatory drive, respiratory muscle weakness, obesity or sleep-disordered breathing context, sedatives, and coma reduce alveolar ventilation and raise hypercapnic respiratory failure risk.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Bradycardic low-output and effusive cardiovascular stress
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Hypometabolism lowers heart rate, contractility, intravascular responsiveness, and pericardial or serous fluid handling, producing bradycardia, low cardiac output, hypotension, effusions, QT prolongation, and shock risk.
Low cardiac output, reduced renal perfusion, impaired free-water clearance, and nonosmotic ADH activity lower serum sodium and can worsen encephalopathy.

Dermal and interstitial glycosaminoglycan accumulation plus smooth-muscle hypomotility produces nonpitting edema, coarse facies, macroglossia, dry skin, delayed reflex relaxation, constipation, ileus, and muscle enzyme elevation.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Stress, cortisol, and glucose reserve failure
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Critical illness, possible adrenal insufficiency or pituitary disease, low gluconeogenic reserve, and reduced drug clearance increase hypoglycemia, pressor-refractory shock, and intolerance of thyroid hormone replacement.
Hypothermia, bradycardia, hypotension, hypercapnia, hyponatremia, hypoglycemia, infection, renal injury, and delayed hormone replacement accumulate into short-term death risk.

supportive_care: Preserve the chronology of severe hypothyroidism, thyroid hormone interruption or malabsorption, and the acute precipitating stress; do not encode the trigger as part of the disease name.

Use presentation-time temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, mental status, respiratory rate, oxygenation, blood gas CO2, sodium, glucose, creatinine, BUN, CK, free T4, TSH, T3, cortisol, ECG, echocardiography, and effusion imaging as ordinary evidence when available.

Parent/satellite structure matters: mental_status_abnormality_presence is the parent for coma severity and GCS; hypothermia_presence is the parent for hypothermia severity; bradycardia_presence is the parent for bradycardia severity; hypoventilation_presence is the parent for hypoventilation severity; effusion presence axes are parents for extent axes.
Do not let absent fever erase infection evidence; myxedema physiology can blunt fever while infection still acts through its own manifold or trigger context.
Assess adrenal reserve context early, but do not turn adrenal crisis into a disease-name qualifier for myxedema coma.

Trend temperature, MAP, heart rate and rhythm, mental status, airway protection, PaCO2, oxygenation, sodium correction rate, glucose, creatinine, urine output, CK, and thyroid hormone levels during early treatment.
Avoid uncontrolled rapid sodium correction, excessive sedation, unsafe oral intake in coma or ileus, and overly aggressive rewarming or fluid loading without cardiac and respiratory context.

Competing diagnoses such as sepsis, adrenal crisis, severe hypoglycemia, stroke, intoxication, hypothermia exposure, acute heart failure, and hyponatremia remain separate evidence paths; overlapping coma, hypothermia, bradycardia, shock, and respiratory failure evidence should not be deleted.
quality_notes: The disease-specific input used for this distillation is only the disease name: Myxedema coma.
Exactly one derived_hazard axis is present: mortality_hazard_in_D-MYXEDEMA-COMA.
Event hazards are used for respiratory failure, aspiration pneumonia, cardiogenic shock, arrhythmia, cardiac arrest, hyponatremic encephalopathy, hypoglycemia, seizure, AKI, and mortality pathways.
Observed findings use parent finding plus satellite or measurement roles for mental status, hypothermia, bradycardia, hypoventilation, edema, effusions, constipation, ileus, and rhabdomyolysis.
No treatment-ranking label fields are used.

Trigger, cause, severity, central versus primary physiology, adrenal reserve, infection, cold exposure, and sedative exposure are represented as context axes or risk factors, not disease-name qualifiers.
